1: # Agentic ODI 🚀
2: 
3: [![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
4: 
5: > **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**
6: 
7: ## 🌟 The Vision: Context-Aware Innovation
8: 
9: **Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)**, built on the "Jobs-to-be-Done" theory, relies on deeply understanding customer needs, desired outcomes, and execution contexts. Historically, applying ODI requires meticulous research, structured data modeling, and rigorous analysis.
10: 
11: **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** represents a paradigm shift in how AI systems consume and reason over external context. By adopting MCP, we can bridge the gap between static user research and dynamic, agentic AI. 
12: 
13: The vision for **Agentic ODI** is to build a unified, open protocol where LLMs and autonomous agents can natively query, understand, and reason over ODI data (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores) dynamically in real-time. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server will act as the "brain" of customer needs, allowing agents to invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions strictly anchored in verified user outcomes.
14: 
15: ## 🏗️ Current State (Experimental Testbed)
16: 
17: This repository serves as an initial sandbox for understanding server-client MCP communication streams. We are utilizing [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) to prototype HTTP-based context delivery.
18: 
19: ### Code Overview
20: 
21: This repository is a [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) made up of six installable packages, each with its own `pyproject.toml`, `src/` layout, and tests:
22: 
23: - **`core/`** (`agentic-odi-core`): Core domain models, repository abstractions, and the event-sourced IntentStore for Jobs, Steps, Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes with ODI opportunity-score computation.
24: - **`mcp_server/`** (`agentic-odi-mcp-server`): FastMCP-based MCP server exposing ODI tools and resources over HTTP. Hosts tools for Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes.
25: - **`local_server/`** (`agentic-odi-local-server`): Local, in-process adapter used by CLI to act as an MCP client while using the same repository layer.
26: - **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`): A [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based command-line interface. It provides a non-MCP entry point for interacting with Agentic ODI and also wraps the MCP server for certain operations.
27: - **`client/`** (`agentic-odi-client`): A Python-based agent client that communicates with the MCP server, executing tool calls over the active connection. It also hosts `run.py`, the local dev launcher that starts the server and the Streamlit UI together.
28: - **`connectors/`** (`agentic-odi-connectors`): Pluggable external integrations (ingest connectors). The first connector is an HTTP MCP **client** that can ingest resources from external MCP servers into the ODI store.
29: 
30: ## 🚀 Getting Started
31: 
32: ### Prerequisites
33: 
34: Python 3.10+ and [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). Install the whole workspace (all packages plus dev tooling):
35: 
36: ```bash
37: uv sync --all-packages
38: ```
39: 
40: This creates a `.venv` and installs `agentic-odi-core`, `agentic-odi-mcp-server`, `agentic-odi-local-server`, `agentic-odi-client`, `agentic-odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi-connectors` in editable mode.
41: 
42: ### Running the Environment
43: 
44: #### 🧰 Command-line interface (CLI)
45: 
46: Agentic ODI ships a [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based CLI so you can interact with the project directly from your terminal — no MCP client or chat UI required. Today it provides version/help plus commands for Customer Outcomes (`agentic-odi outcomes ...`) and external MCP connectors (`agentic-odi connectors ...`), giving you a scriptable, automation-friendly alternative to the MCP/chat path.
47: 
48: Launch it with:
49: 
50: ```bash
51: python -m cli --version   # print the Agentic ODI version
52: python -m cli --help      # show available options and commands
53: python -m cli             # show help when no command is given
54: ```
55: 
56: A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way.
57: 
58: #### Manage Customer Outcomes
59: 
60: Manage Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value) via the CLI. The CLI acts as an MCP client, so the server must be running (`python -m mcp_server`):
61: 
62: ```bash
63: # Add a Customer Outcome
64: agentic-odi outcomes add --job-id <job-id>   --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors"   --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding"   --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2   --category cost_reduction   --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn"
65: 
66: # List outcomes (optionally filtered)
67: agentic-odi outcomes list
68: agentic-odi outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
69: 
70: # Get, update, delete
71: agentic-odi outcomes get <outcome-id>
72: agentic-odi outcomes update <outcome-id> --importance 9.0
73: agentic-odi outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes
74: 
75: # Compute ODI Opportunity Score
76: agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2
77: ```
78: 
79: Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` to point to a non-default server if needed.
80: 
81: ### External connectors (MCP ingest)
82: 
83: The `connectors/` package enables ingesting external resources via MCP. Configure connectors via `--config` (default: `.agentic-odi/connectors.json`).
84: 
85: ```bash
86: # List configured connectors
87: agentic-odi connectors list
88: agentic-odi connectors list --config /path/to/connectors.json
89: 
90: # Add an HTTP MCP connector
91: agentic-odi connectors add mcp --name my-connector --url http://localhost:9000/mcp
92: 
93: # Check connector health
94: agentic-odi connectors health --name my-connector
95: 
96: # Ingest resources from the connector into the local store (idempotent by URI)
97: agentic-odi connectors ingest --name my-connector
98: ```
99: 
100: 
101: 
102: #### ⚡ One-command launch (recommended)
103: 
104: `python -m client.run` starts both the MCP server and the Streamlit UI concurrently. Press **Ctrl+C** to stop both.
105: 
106: ```bash
107: python -m client.run
108: ```
109: 
110: | Service | URL |
111: |---|---|
112: | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp |
113: | Streamlit Chat UI | http://localhost:8501 |
114: 
115: #### 🔧 Manual split-terminal (alternative)
116: 
117: Open two terminals and run each process separately:
118: 
119: ```bash
120: # Terminal 1 — MCP server
121: python -m mcp_server
122: 
123: # Terminal 2 — Streamlit chat UI
124: streamlit run client/src/client/app.py
125: ```
126: 
127: ### Local tools-capable LLM backend (for MCP testing)
128: 
129: To exercise real tool-calling end-to-end against the MCP server, you need a local LLM backend that:
130: 
131: - Exposes an **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API** (for example, `/v1/chat/completions`), and
132: - Supports OpenAI-style **`tools` / `tool_calls`**.
133: 
134: A simple fully local option is [`llama-cpp-python`](https://github.com/abetlen/llama-cpp-python), which can run a quantized model on your machine and expose an OpenAI-compatible server.
135: 
136: 1. **Install a local LLM server**
137: 
138:    Install `llama-cpp-python` in your environment (see its README for platform-specific build notes):
139: 
140:    ```bash
141:    pip install llama-cpp-python
142:    ```
143: 
144: 2. **Download a small tools-capable model**
145: 
146:    Download a small GGUF model that supports function/tool calling (for example, a 7B function-calling variant from Hugging Face) and note its path, e.g. `C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf`.
147: 
148: 3. **Start the OpenAI-compatible server**
149: 
150:    Start the server and give the model a friendly alias that matches the default used by the Streamlit client (`client/src/client/app.py`):
151: 
152:    ```bash
153:    python -m llama_cpp.server \
154:      --model "C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf" \
155:      --model_alias local-tools-model \
156:      --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 \
157:      --chat_format openai
158:    ```
159: 
160:    This exposes an OpenAI-style API at `http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1`.
161: 
162: 4. **Point the Streamlit client at the local server**
163: 
164:    `client/src/client/app.py` reads defaults from environment variables (with sensible fallbacks):
165: 
166:    - `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` (default: `http://localhost:8001/v1`)
167:    - `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` (default: `local`)
168:    - `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` (default: `local-tools-model`)
169:    - `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` (default: `http://localhost:8000/mcp`)
170: 
171:    You can either set these in your shell or adjust them in the Streamlit sidebar under **“LLM Configuration”**.
172: 
173: 5. **Verify tool-calling against the MCP server**
174: 
175:    - (Optional) Before starting the UI, you can quickly verify that the LLM backend is reachable:
176: 
177:      ```bash
178:      curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/models
179:      ```
180: 
181:      If this request fails, fix your local LLM server configuration before debugging the MCP client/server.
182: 
183:    - Start the MCP server and Streamlit UI (either via `python -m client.run` or the split-terminal commands above).
184:    - In the browser UI, ask the assistant something that should use ODI tools, for example: “Help me define a new Job-to-be-Done and add it to your ODI repository.”
185:    - You should see the assistant briefly display that it is calling tools (for example, `add_job`, `get_jobs`, etc.) and then respond with grounded ODI guidance, confirming that the local LLM, MCP server, and client wiring all work together.
186:    - If the LLM backend is unreachable or misconfigured, the UI will show a clear error banner indicating that the backend at your configured **Base URL** could not be reached, along with details from the underlying error. Use that message together with the steps above to fix your local LLM setup.
187: 
188: #### 🤖 Agent-driven testing
189: 
190: Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it will start both processes, open the browser, send a test message, and report the results.
191: 
192: ## 🧪 Testing
193: 
194: Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely in-memory — no running server required. Each project owns its tests. CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12** and stores a coverage report as a build artifact:
195: 
196: ```bash
197: uv run --directory core pytest
198: uv run --directory mcp_server pytest
199: uv run --directory local_server pytest
200: uv run --directory client pytest
201: uv run --directory cli pytest
202: uv run --directory connectors pytest
203: ```
204: 
205: ### 🧠 Agent session tracking
206: 
207: Agent sessions are captured with the [Entire](https://docs.entire.io/overview) CLI. The repository integration lives in `.entire/settings.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, and `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`. Run `entire status` to confirm it is enabled and `entire checkpoint list` to inspect captured checkpoints.
208: 
209: ### 🧹 Linting, formatting & type checks (CI parity)
210: 
211: The CI pipeline runs several quality checks. You can mirror them locally with:
212: 
213: ```bash
214: # Ruff lint and formatting checks (per-file config comes from each project's pyproject.toml)
215: uv run ruff check .
216: uv run ruff format --check .
217: 
218: # Type checking (run per project so each project's config applies)
219: uv run --directory core mypy .
220: uv run --directory mcp_server mypy .
221: uv run --directory local_server mypy .
222: uv run --directory client mypy .
223: uv run --directory cli mypy .
224: uv run --directory connectors mypy .
225: 
226: # Security scanning
227: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r cli/src client/src core/src local_server/src mcp_server/src connectors/src
228: 
229: # Tests (same as CI)
230: uv run --directory core pytest
231: uv run --directory mcp_server pytest
232: uv run --directory local_server pytest
233: uv run --directory client pytest
234: uv run --directory cli pytest
235: uv run --directory connectors pytest
236: ```
237: 
238: To run these automatically before each commit, you can enable the bundled pre-commit hooks:
239: 
240: ```bash
241: uv tool install pre-commit
242: pre-commit install
243: ```
244: 
245: After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` will run on staged files whenever you commit. You can also trigger them manually with:
246: 
247: ```bash
248: pre-commit run --all-files
249: ```
250: 
251: ### 🧼 Developer workflow for formatting
252: 
253: - **When editing Python files**, either:
254:   - Rely on the **pre-commit hooks** above (recommended), or
255:   - Run Ruff formatting directly before pushing:
256: 
257:     ```bash
258:     uv run ruff format .
259:     ```
260: 
261: - **CI behavior**:
262:   - CI runs `uv run ruff check .` to lint without modifying files.
263:   - CI runs `uv run ruff format --check .` to *verify* formatting only.
264:   - If CI fails on formatting, run `uv run ruff format .` locally, commit the changes, and push again.
265:
